scope_covered: Bibliography, first group (21 keys: variance reduction, finite sums, classical theory). For each key: bib entry checked against arXiv API, Crossref, PMLR/JMLR/NeurIPS metadata; every sentence citing it (grep) checked against the opened source text (PDFs downloaded and read). Precise references opened: Arjevani et al. Theorem 8 (JMLR), Mokhtari et al. Corollary 3, Hofmann et al. Theorem 1/Corollary 1, Bach Proposition 5.9 and Section 5.4.4 (online version), Zhang-Yin Definition 2, Na et al. Section 5, Dragomir et al. Corollary 1, Yang et al. Assumption 1, Qin et al. Algorithm 2/Theorem 4.1, Finito Section 3, Driggs et al. B-SAGA, Xiao-Zhang weighted sampling, Mairal eq. (3.8)/Prop. 3.4, Katyusha Section 6. One numeric check (MISO identity, DIAG threshold).

checked_ok.claim: 'the step of hofmann2015variance' (best step of the proof)
checked_ok.evidence: arXiv 1506.03662 v4, Theorem 1: gamma*(K)=a*(K)/(4L), a*(K)=2K/(1+K+sqrt(1+K^2)), K=4qL/(n mu); Corollary 1: 'rho is maximized for gamma = gamma*(K)'. (Equality with the best step of Prop. 5.9's proof checked by math-saga.)

checked_ok.claim: yang2014data, gonen2016solving = 'preconditioning where the loss curvature is bounded below'; Yang = 'a preconditioner computed once'
checked_ok.evidence: Yang et al. Assumption 1: 'l''(z,y) >= beta for |z| <= r'; preconditioner H = rho I + C, rho = lambda/beta, then SAG/SVRG on preconditioned data. Gonen et al.: 'a novel preconditioning method for ridge regression ... equipping SVRG with this preconditioning'.

checked_ok.claim: qin2023convergence = 'SVRG anchors under reshuffling, without linear rate' (sign steps)
checked_ok.evidence: arXiv 2310.15976 v4 Algorithm 2 SignRVR: v = grad f_pi(x) - grad f_pi(y_t) + grad f(y_t), y_t anchor at the start of each reshuffled epoch; Theorem 4.1: pathwise descent inequality, nonconvex stationarity bound, no linear rate. SignRVR already in v1 (2023).

checked_ok.claim: ying2017variance, park2020linear = linear rates under reshuffled / cyclic orders
checked_ok.evidence: Ying et al. abstract: 'the first theoretical guarantee of linear convergence under random reshuffling for SAGA', Theorem 1; Park-Ryu abstract: 'We prove C-SAGA converges linearly', C-SAGA = cyclic SAGA.

checked_ok.claim: defazio2014finito = 'a permutation order was seen to help'
checked_ok.evidence: Finito PMLR PDF Sec. 3: 'this approach does not give any speedup with SAG, however it works spectacularly well with Finito. We see speedups of up to a factor of two'; SAGA paper: 'per-pass re-permuted access ordering, empirical speed-ups of up-to a factor of 2x'.
arXiv 1906.01133: 'grad~^{B-SAGA} = (1/theta)(grad f_j(x_k) - grad f_j(phi_j)) + (1/n) sum_i grad f_i(phi_i) ... When theta = n ... recovers the SAG gradient estimator'.
arXiv 1403.4699: 'When the sampling probabilities for f_i are proportional to their Lipschitz constants ... O((n + L_avg/mu) log(1/eps))'.

findings.claim: linear rates are proved for reshuffled and cyclic orders \cite{ying2017variance,park2020linear}, some beating $e^{-1}$ per pass for $\kappa<4.08$ \cite{mokhtari2018surpassing}.
findings.problem: The threshold 4.08 and the comparison with the memory factor e^{-1} are the authors' computation, not a statement of the cited source; 'some' suggests several proved rates do it, whereas among the cited sources only DIAG's does (Ying et al. and Park-Ryu prove 1-O(1/kappa^2) per pass).
findings.evidence: Mokhtari et al. (arXiv 1611.00347 v2) Corollary 3: ||x^{n(m-1)+1}-x*|| <= rho^m[1-(1-rho)/n min{1,(n-1)/2}]||x0-x*||, rho=(kappa-1)/(kappa+1), cyclic order; no occurrence of e^{-1}, 4.08 or of a comparison with i.i.d. sampling in the text. rho^2<e^{-1} iff kappa<(sqrt e+1)/(sqrt e-1)=4.08299 (checks/cite-vr_miso_and_diag.py). Repository note theory/B4_sampling_order.tex l. 515: 'a comparison that these papers do not make'.
findings.proposed_fix: linear rates are proved for reshuffled and cyclic orders \cite{ying2017variance,park2020linear}, and that of cyclic DIAG, $\frac{\kappa-1}{\kappa+1}$ per pass on the distance \cite[Corollary~3]{mokhtari2018surpassing}, beats $e^{-1}$ for $\kappa<4.08$ (our comparison).

findings.problem: DIAG (mokhtari2018surpassing) is a fixed cyclic-order method, not a reshuffled one.
findings.evidence: Mokhtari et al., after Lemma 1: 'The cyclic scheme is critical in proving the result in (21) ... If we pick functions uniformly at random, as in MISO, it is not possible to write the expression in (21)'; title: 'A Cyclic Incremental Method'.

findings.problem: c_bar is defined nowhere in the paper; in the code it is the upper curvature bound c_loss (0.5 softmax, 1 least squares), whereas the cited preconditioner uses a LOWER bound beta of the loss curvature (H = C + (lambda/beta) I). The metric is a variant of the source's, not the source's; they coincide for least squares.
findings.evidence: grep: single occurrence of \bar c in the .tex; muon/lab/vrmuon.py l. 641-649 ('model Hessian c_l Sigma_hat + lam I'), muon/lab/problems.py l. 319, 415; Yang et al. arXiv 1408.3115 v4 Assumption 1 'l''(z,y) >= beta' and 'H = rho I + C, where rho = lambda/beta'.
findings.proposed_fix: the feature-covariance metric $\omega\mapsto\omega(\bar c\hat\Sigma+\lambda I)^{-1}$, $\bar c=\max_ic_i$ (\cite{yang2014data} use a lower bound of the loss curvature in its place)

findings.problem: Zhang-Yin's RSI constant nu is a single lower bound valid for all x; mu_eff(theta) is the pointwise ratio, whose infimum is the best RSI constant.
findings.evidence: arXiv 1303.4645 v2, Definition 2: 'satisfies the restricted secant inequality (RSI) with constant nu > 0 if ... <grad f(x), x - x_prj> >= nu ||x - x_prj||^2'.
findings.proposed_fix: (the pointwise ratio of the restricted secant inequality of \cite{zhang2013gradient})

findings.claim: Proposition~5.9 holds in any fixed metric $P$ with $R_P^2,\mu_P$ \cite{dragomir2021fast}
findings.problem: The source certifies a Bregman SAGA in a fixed (quadratic) metric with its own constants (1/8, 1/2), not Proposition 5.9; the transfer of Proposition 5.9 is a change of variables.
findings.evidence: arXiv 2104.09813, Corollary 1: 'If nabla^2 h is constant (h is quadratic) ... E[psi_t] <= (1 - min(1/(8 kappa_{f/h}), 1/(2n)))^t psi_0'.
findings.proposed_fix: Proposition~5.9 holds in any fixed metric $P$ with $R_P^2,\mu_P$ (a change of variables; cf.\ \cite[Corollary~1]{dragomir2021fast})
